claim: Authority can only shrink as it is delegated — each link in a chain may hold a subset of what the link before it held, never a capability its delegator did not have.

steps.label: a chain that narrows at every link
steps.evidence: may read: True; may write: False

steps.label: a sub-agent claiming more than its delegator held
steps.note: Without this rule, delegation is a laundering step: the sub-agent asks for more than its delegator could have, and nothing downstream can tell the difference.

steps.label: a capability re-acquired four links down
steps.evidence: the denial names the capability and the depth

steps.label: a loop back to an earlier actor
steps.note: A loop lets authority be re-derived from a later link, which is amplification wearing a longer path.

steps.label: a near-miss capability name
steps.note: Names are compared exactly. A gate that read structure into them would turn every new capability name into a silent policy change.

steps.label: delegating the work while delegating no authority
steps.note: A correct answer, not an error: an agent may be asked to do something and given no authority to act on its own.
